Subject: Supplier portal invite blocked by spoof detection – needs OTP fallback

Hi Luis,

I set up your BlueHarbor account in our Coupa tenant this morning and sent the invite to luis.reyes@blueharbor.com and procurement@blueharbor.com. Sam on your side replied that the invite fails with a red banner: "Potentially spoofed invitation" and the account creation never completes. Screenshot attached.

Two quick asks so we can get you live ASAP:
- Can you confirm whether procurement@blueharbor.com is a shared mailbox (alias) vs a distinct mailbox? Shared aliases usually cause header mismatches that trigger our anti-spoof rules.
- If you have a phone number on file for procurement (or a mobile for the user), we can enable an OTP fallback in Coupa while we sort sender headers. That often bypasses the browser-level reject and lets people accept the invite.

I copied Ben to help escalate with Platform/ops if we need to change the sender envelope or whitelist a sending domain.

Thanks — sorry for the friction.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales (Procurement)
Redwood Inference
ava@redwood.com

Marissa / Ops team — forwarding BlueHarbor thread. Their invite is being rejected by Coupa as a spoofed invite. Quick notes from troubleshooting:
- Likely culprit: display-name (Ava/Redwood) != SMTP MAIL FROM / DKIM results in a reputation/anti-spoof rule firing.
- BlueHarbor uses a distribution alias (procurement@) which can obscure Recipient vs Alias — that sometimes triggers heuristics.

Marissa, can you:
1) Check JIRA-OPS-1294 for whether we have a pending whitelist for invitations@redwood-invite.com or redwood-smtp1.redwood.com.
2) If possible, resend invite from invitations@redwood-invite.com (single consistent envelope) and enable the OTP fallback for that tenant (Coupa setting).
3) If resend fails, escalate to Coupa support and share raw SMTP headers (I attached raw_smtp-headers.txt).

I put Ava in the loop to coordinate with the vendor. Let me know if you want me to call Coupa support directly.

— Ben

Hi Luis — Marissa from Platform Ops here. Thanks for the details and the screenshot.

What we changed this morning:
- Whitelisted invitations@redwood-invite.com in the Coupa tenant for BlueHarbor Components and aligned the sender envelope to use that single address.
- Enabled an OTP (SMS) fallback for the tenant; you should now see an option to receive a code if the browser blocks the direct accept flow.
- Cleared a stale DKIM signature that was failing for some outbound invites — that was likely the root cause of the spoof heuristic.

Action for you: please try the new invite I just re-sent (subject: "BlueHarbor Components — Redwood portal invite"). If the browser still shows a warning, try in an incognito window or clear cookies for coupa.com. If that still fails, reply with the timestamp you attempted and I'll open an expedited Coupa case.

I attached the raw SMTP headers we captured for your diagnostic team.

Apologies for the hassle — we want your PO setup live before your first PCard cycle next week.

Best,
